title: What federal inspectors general found at San Francisco grantees
question: Have federal auditors found problems at organisations that also take City money?
finding: Two City-funded nonprofits had serious findings. In June 2026 the Justice Department's inspector general questioned $579,145 of Huckleberry Youth Programs' victim-assistance spending and $145,433 of its match, found it could not track spending by funding source, and found part of the match was paid with a City grant that was federal money, which the rules forbid; the City paid Huckleberry $30.3 million in fiscal 2019-2026. In 2016 it found Asian Pacific Islander Legal Outreach had commingled grant funds and overstated victims served (203 reported, 92 supported), and questioned $500,000 of drawn costs. A separate $455,000 award remained undrawn at the cutoff; a City supplier named Nihonmachi Legal Outreach dba API Legal (name match) was paid $16.4 million in fiscal 2019-2026. The federal transit audits also questioned costs at SFMTA for procurement in FY2017 and cash management in FY2019.
how: Figures and findings read from each report's summary; City payments from the organisation profiles.
limits: The August 2026 open recommendation register still lists the Huckleberry monetary recommendation as resolved, meaning management agreed on action. A final determination of allowed costs or repayment is not established. The 2016 report predates the City payments shown, and the City supplier is linked to the audited organisation by name only. GAO-20-433 was requested as a San Francisco case study, but it is not one.

rows.subject: Huckleberry Youth Programs, Inc. (victim-assistance subawards via the State)
rows.said: Questioned $579,145 of $705,448 subawarded and $145,433 of match; part of the match was paid with a City grant that was itself federal money.

rows.subject: Asian Pacific Islander Legal Outreach (two Justice Department grants)
rows.said: Auditors questioned $500,000 of drawn costs; a separate $455,000 award had no drawdowns at the cutoff. The August 2026 OIG register lists no open recommendation for the audit’s publication month. Cash repayment was not reported. The grantee reported 203 victims served where records supported 92.
rows.org: Nihonmachi Legal Outreach dba API Legal (name match)

rows.subject: University of California, San Francisco (incurred costs on NSF awards)
rows.said: Audit of 20 awards: UCSF agreed to reimburse or credit $36,980 of $136,810 questioned. NSF ultimately disallowed $79,144. Its March 2025 final-action table records the remaining $77,792 as repaid and all six then-open recommendations closed.

rows.subject: San Francisco State University (incurred costs)
rows.said: San Francisco State agreed with all findings. In its March 2024 final-action table NSF recorded the $260 disallowed as repaid and all six recommendations closed.

rows.subject: EPA oversight of San Francisco Bay Water Quality Improvement Fund grants
rows.said: Weak monitoring by EPA put $3.5 million of remaining funds in four sampled grants at risk; no City body among the sampled recipients.

rows.subject: Quality review of the Metropolitan Transportation Commission single audit, fiscal 2017
rows.said: Audit work reliable; $75.7 million of federal transport money spent; one reporting-package deficiency corrected.

rows.subject: Security of federal computer systems at San Francisco International Airport
rows.said: Federal components agreed with 21 of 23 recommendations; the systems are federal, not the Airport's.

rows.subject: GAO-20-433, homelessness counts and HUD oversight
rows.said: National report; San Francisco is named 2 time(s), as a coastal city with rising homelessness. GAO visited Colorado Springs, Los Angeles, and New York; there is no San Francisco case study.

rows.subject: GAO-17-204, immigration-status checks for benefits (SAVE)
rows.said: National report; San Francisco is named 0 times.

rows.subject: SFMTA single audit FY2017, finding 2017-001
rows.said: The inspector general recommended that the Federal Transit Administration ensure compliance and recover the questioned funds if appropriate. The tracker lists both recommendations as closed.

link.t: SA2018067, printed page 3, recommendations A1 and A2

rows.subject: SFMTA single audit FY2019, finding 2019-001
rows.said: KPMG found inadequate controls over SFMTA requests for federal transit money. It recommended management review reimbursement reports before submission and reinforce reimbursement procedures. In its FY2020 filing, SFMTA reported that the ineligible amounts and applicable refunds were netted against a subsequent federal draw. It sought guidance on $1,682 of estimated interest.
